facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: KBR enters the cut-off with a moderately levered balance sheet, drifting toward lower reported leverage, and a perimeter about to change. On management's own measure, net debt of 2,118 against trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA of 1,015 gives 2.1x at October 2, 2026, compared with 2.2x at January 2, 2026, 2.3x at April 3, 2026 and 2.3x at July 3, 2026. Gross debt principal was 2,557 at October 2, 2026, made up of 957 Term Loan A, 975 Term Loan B, 250 of 4.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and 375 drawn on the 1,000 revolver. On the same earnings measure gross leverage is 2.52x and net leverage is 2.09x. Those ratios carry a definition risk that matters for the credit view. Beginning with the first quarter of fiscal 2026, adjusted EBITDA was revised to add back the group's share of joint venture interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization and acquisition costs, prospectively and without recasting history; the add-back is 44 over nine months of fiscal 2026. Removing it gives trailing EBITDA of 971 and net leverage of 2.18x, which is almost level with the 2.19x computed for fiscal 2025, so nearly all of the reported improvement reflects the change of definition. The measure also adds back spin-off, acquisition and restructuring costs of 72 over nine months (18 a year earlier), and starts from operating income that includes equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates of 167 against cash distributions of earnings of 145. A plain operating income plus depreciation and amortization proxy for the trailing twelve months is 895, which gives net leverage of 2.37x on this unadjusted basis.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The first scheduled wall is near. Current maturities of long-term debt are 554 at October 2, 2026, against 49 at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; Senior Notes follow in September 2028 and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029. The refinancing sits alongside the planned spin-off targeted for January 4, 2027, after which management intends to use cash distributed by the MTS business to reduce debt; the amount, the post-spin debt and the post-spin earnings are not supplied. For scale, MTS carried 441 of nine-month adjusted EBITDA out of 777, and the other segment plus corporate carried 336. Operating cash flow of 331 for nine months fiscal 2026 compares with 506 a year earlier. Receivable monetization programs sold 935 in the period and settled 935, leaving 65 outstanding, the same as at the start of the year, so the programs did not add net funding over nine months but remain a recurring working capital tool. Claims outside the debt figure include operating and finance leases, a 41 Kuwait court judgment under appeal that is not accrued, letters of credit and surety support, and a United Kingdom pension surplus rather than a deficit. The view is therefore moderate leverage, adequate liquidity, a near-term amortization step, an EBITDA definition that flatters the trend, and a covenant package that cannot be tested against defined terms.

facts.label: Covenants and compliance
facts.text: The Senior Credit Facility has two maintenance tests as the filings describe them: [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:19] "may not exceed 4.25 to 1 in 2023, reducing to 4.00 to 1 in 2024 and thereafter" for consolidated net leverage and [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:19] "may not be less than 3.00 to 1 as of the last day of any fiscal quarter" for consolidated interest coverage. Compliance is stated for every reported date, most recently [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:19] "As of October 2, 2026, we were in compliance with our financial covenants under our Senior Credit Facility." The reported covenant ratio is not printed. On the company basis computed here, net leverage of 2.09x sits below the described 4.00x ceiling and interest expense cover of 7.00x sits above the 3.00x floor; both are indicative only because the defined terms, any amendment effect from Amendment No. 14 and the treatment of joint venture add-backs are not available. The margin grid on the revolver and Term Loan A steps at net leverage of 4.25x, 3.25x, 2.25x and 1.25x, so the indicative 2.09x level would place pricing in the band below 2.25x, subject to the defined ratio.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The transaction that dominates the credit view is the Planned Spin-Off of MTS into a separate listed company, to be named Trinzic, Inc., first announced in September 2025 and now targeted for January 4, 2027, the first business day of fiscal 2027, after the evidence cutoff. Completion is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing, and regulatory approvals. The mechanism that matters to creditors is that MTS is the larger segment by revenue, adjusted EBITDA and backlog, so after separation the remaining KBR group is the STS business plus corporate costs, while management says it will use cash distributed by MTS from its own financing to reduce KBR's debt. The size of that distribution, which debt stays with which company, whether the Senior Credit Facility and the Senior Notes remain with KBR, and the covenant and guarantor perimeter after separation are not supplied. The July 29, 2026 Amendment No. 14 to the credit agreement permits the internal reorganization; its text is not supplied. Behaviour to date is that of a company preparing a separation while keeping its dividend, cutting buybacks, and making small acquisitions and minority investments, with no documented priming, non-pro-rata exchange or distribution to insiders. The creditor view is therefore: a business with diversified government and commercial exposure, moderate leverage and large pending structural change, where the post-spin perimeter, debt allocation and covenant package, not the pre-spin credit statistics, will decide the credit quality, and where those facts are not yet in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The one transaction in the pack is the Planned Spin-Off of the Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business into Trinzic, Inc., announced in September 2025 and targeted for January 4, 2027, after the evidence cutoff. It is a spin-off to shareholders, not a sale, merger or sponsor transaction, so there is no purchase price, sponsor equity or acquisition financing. It is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of the Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing and regulatory approvals. For creditors, the mechanism is that MTS makes a cash distribution to KBR from its own financing before completion, which management intends to use to reduce KBR's debt; the amount, the debt that stays with each company and the treatment of guarantors, liens and covenants are not supplied. Spin-off costs and other charges were 24 in the third quarter and 70 over nine months fiscal 2026. No new notes, term loan or other debt issue by KBR, INC. appears in the periods covered: the financing events are revolver borrowings of 281 and repayments of 301, scheduled repayments of 29 on Term Loan A and 8 on Term Loan B, and Amendment No. 14 to the Credit Agreement dated July 29, 2026, which permits internal reorganization transactions for the spin-off and makes other modifications that are not described. Management states that the spin-off is tax-free in intent, and that KBR and Trinzic expect to launch as independent companies in January, which is Management Language. citations.quote: The one transaction in the pack is the Planned Spin-Off of the Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business into Trinzic, Inc., announced in September 2025 and targeted for January 4, 2027, after the evidence cutoff. It is a spin-off to shareholders, not a sale, merger or sponsor transaction, so there is no purchase price, sponsor equity or acquisition financing. It is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of the Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing and regulatory approvals. For creditors, the mechanism is that MTS makes a cash distribution to KBR from its own financing before completion, which management intends to use to reduce KBR's debt; the amount, the debt that stays with each company and the treatment of guarantors, liens and covenants are not supplied. Spin-off costs and other charges were 24 in the third quarter and 70 over nine months fiscal 2026. No new notes, term loan or other debt issue by KBR, INC. appears in the periods covered: the financing events are revolver borrowings of 281 and repayments of 301, scheduled repayments of 29 on Term Loan A and 8 on Term Loan B, and Amendment No. 14 to the Credit Agreement dated July 29, 2026, which permits internal reorganization transactions for the spin-off and makes other modifications that are not described. Management states that the spin-off is tax-free in intent, and that KBR and Trinzic expect to launch as independent companies in January, which is Management Language. Liquidity effects, debt maturities and covenant levels are in the financial base module. The spin-off is conditional on financing, tax opinions and a Form 10 becoming effective, and management says it will use cash distributed by the segment to reduce debt.
Backlog was 17,718 at October 2, 2026, with 38% executable within one year, and nearly all contracts can be terminated for convenience.
Documented actions show lower buybacks, steady dividends, small acquisitions and a covenant amendment to permit reorganization, with no priming or distribution to insiders.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: KBR, INC. is a moderately levered, well-funded defense and sustainable-technology services group whose credit is sound on today's numbers but is about to be reset by the planned spin-off of its larger segment. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,046 million, net leverage of 2.1x on management's measure and a backlog of USD 17,718 million. The weakest point is that adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026, current maturities rose to USD 554 million, and no post-spin debt, covenant or guarantor terms are disclosed. The outcome turns on how much debt the Mission Technology Solutions cash distribution retires, how the August 2027 term loan is refinanced, and whether the remaining sustainable technology group can carry the capital structure it inherits.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. The spin-off, not the pre-spin ratios, drives the credit view (Documentary Fact for the facts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). The planned separation of Mission Technology Solutions into Trinzic, Inc. is targeted for January 4, 2027, after the cutoff, and is conditional on Board approval, tax treatment, a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, financing and regulatory approvals [business context, transaction register]. That segment carried USD 3,870 million of USD 5,935 million nine-month revenue and USD 441 million of USD 777 million nine-month adjusted EBITDA [business context, calculations], so what remains is the sustainable technology segment plus corporate costs, with USD 336 million of nine-month adjusted EBITDA on the same definition. Management intends to use cash distributed by the departing segment to reduce KBR's debt, but the amount, the allocation of existing debt, and the fate of guarantors and covenants are Not supplied [business context, gaps]. Credit implication: pre-spin leverage cannot be carried forward, and no post-spin leverage claim is made here.

facts.text: 3. A refinancing and amortization step falls inside twelve months (Documentary Fact). Current maturities of long-term debt are USD 554 million at October 2, 2026 against USD 49 million at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; the USD 250 million Senior Notes mature in September 2028, and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029 [financial base, debt schedule]. Liquidity is USD 1,046 million, made of cash of USD 439 million and USD 607 million undrawn on the revolver after letters of credit, against the USD 625 million revolver capacity stated in the release [financial base, liquidity chart]. Credit implication: the tranche can be repaid from liquidity or refinanced, but its timing coincides with the separation, when lender consent, ratings and covenant terms are being reset (Amendment No. 14 already permitted the reorganization).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity is a clear strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,046 million of cash and undrawn revolver, against a first scheduled tranche of USD 554 million and no maturity of the Senior Notes until September 2028 [financial base]. Leverage is moderate on every measure computed, from 2.1x as printed to 2.37x unadjusted, well below the described 4.00x covenant ceiling (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only). Revenue visibility from a backlog of USD 17,718 million, with USD 9.0 billion of the Mission Technology Solutions backlog funded and USD 5,404 million of award options (Documentary Fact) [business context]. Diversified end markets and geography beyond the U.S. government, with commercial and infrastructure clients and international government clients contributing USD 2,454 million and USD 905 million in fiscal 2025 (Documentary Fact). Cash returns are discretionary and have been reduced, with USD 402 million of repurchase authorization remaining, which gives management a lever in a stress (Analyst Interpretation). The management description of a low capital intensity model with favorable operating cash flows is Management Language and is not adopted; the financial base shows nine-month capital expenditure of USD 36 million against operating cash flow of USD 331 million, which is consistent with it.

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: The analysis is traceable enough for restricted committee use. Nearly every figure in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis traces to a located page in the pinned filings, and recomputation from separately extracted filing lines reproduced gross debt, net debt, trailing adjusted EBITDA, liquidity and the maturity schedule. The most important provenance gap is covenant compliance and the post-spin structure: the credit agreement, its Amendment No. 14 and the Form 10 are not in the pack, so statements that covenants are met are management assertions and the surviving credit cannot be sized. A second gap is the cash flow attribution, which the cash flow statement does not support as written. The defects found are minor and none changes the credit view. Because the same analyst wrote the modules and this trace, an independent reviewer should repeat the highest-risk checks before the report is used.

Debt is itemized by tranche. Whether it matches the covenant definition is not shown.

Amendment No. 14 is reported but its text is not supplied: [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:17] "We entered into Amendment No. 14 to our Credit Agreement on July 29, 2026". Planned spin-off and use of proceeds: [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:33] "we are targeting completion on January 4, 2027", subject among other conditions to [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:33] "the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form 10 filed with the SEC on September 30, 2026". Management states a debt reduction intention: [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:52] "We intend to use the cash distributed to KBR by the Mission Technology Solutions business to reduce our level of indebtedness." ### Extraction fidelity and parse gaps

Text extraction succeeded for all seven files; extraction success is not a fidelity review. Tables arrive as flattened text lines, so column alignment must be confirmed against the header lines on the same page, and the 10-K debt and covenant pages mix table and narrative text. Page numbers in the citations are chunks of extracted text, not printed pages; the printed page numbers also appear inside the text and differ. The extracted text carries no charts or images, and the releases are text releases rather than slide decks, so no chart, image or speaker-note coverage is claimed. There are no workbooks or scans in the pack.

Fiscal 2026 ends January 1, 2027, after the cutoff. Every figure carries its own period label. Trailing twelve months (TTM) is used only as management defines it for adjusted EBITDA, and for the labelled interest-expense memo in the calculations.

Perimeter: KBR, Inc. consolidated under US GAAP, continuing operations, with the HomeSafe disposal presented as discontinued operations and the Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business still inside continuing operations. No source names a narrower borrower, restricted group or guarantor group; the Senior Credit Facility borrower is KBR, Inc., and the Senior Notes are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries described by class only.

Scope: extract and organize the reported financial base (income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, debt, liquidity, covenants, non-GAAP reconciliations), calculate leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity measures from cited inputs, review definitions, and state what the evidence supports for the modules that follow. No credit rating, valuation or investment recommendation is given here. The Q3 fiscal 2026 10-Q and release are the controlling sources for current balances; the annual report controls fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024.

### Financial base view

KBR enters the cut-off with a moderately levered balance sheet, drifting toward lower reported leverage, and a perimeter about to change. On management's own measure, net debt of 2,118 against trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA of 1,015 gives 2.1x at October 2, 2026, compared with 2.2x at January 2, 2026, 2.3x at April 3, 2026 and 2.3x at July 3, 2026. Gross debt principal was 2,557 at October 2, 2026, made up of 957 Term Loan A, 975 Term Loan B, 250 of 4.750% Senior Notes due 2028 and 375 drawn on the 1,000 revolver. On the same earnings measure gross leverage is 2.52x and net leverage is 2.09x. Those ratios carry a definition risk that matters for the credit view. Beginning with the first quarter of fiscal 2026, adjusted EBITDA was revised to add back the group's share of joint venture interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization and acquisition costs, prospectively and without recasting history; the add-back is 44 over nine months of fiscal 2026. Removing it gives trailing EBITDA of 971 and net leverage of 2.18x, which is almost level with the 2.19x computed for fiscal 2025, so nearly all of the reported improvement reflects the change of definition. The measure also adds back spin-off, acquisition and restructuring costs of 72 over nine months (18 a year earlier), and starts from operating income that includes equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates of 167 against cash distributions of earnings of 145. A plain operating income plus depreciation and amortization proxy for the trailing twelve months is 895, which gives net leverage of 2.37x on this unadjusted basis.

Cover is available on cash interest only for fiscal 2025: adjusted EBITDA of 968 over cash interest paid of 141 gives 6.87x. No 2026 cash interest figure is supplied in the interim sources, so the interim cover cells are Not supplied. As a labelled memo, adjusted EBITDA over interest expense is 7.00x on a trailing basis to October 2, 2026 (interest expense of 145). Liquidity at October 2, 2026 is cash of 439 plus 607 undrawn on the committed revolver after 18 of letters of credit, 1,046 in total. The release states revolver capacity of 625, which is the commitment less borrowings with no deduction for the letters of credit; the 10-Q reports the letters separately. Bilateral and uncommitted lines of 491 can be used for letters of credit only, with 186 unused, and are excluded from liquidity. Of the 439 cash, 67 is joint venture and Aspire Defence project cash and the captive insurer holds part of the domestic balance, so the cash that is freely available is smaller than the headline.

The first scheduled wall is near. Current maturities of long-term debt are 554 at October 2, 2026, against 49 at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; Senior Notes follow in September 2028 and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029. The refinancing sits alongside the planned spin-off targeted for January 4, 2027, after which management intends to use cash distributed by the MTS business to reduce debt; the amount, the post-spin debt and the post-spin earnings are not supplied. For scale, MTS carried 441 of nine-month adjusted EBITDA out of 777, and the other segment plus corporate carried 336. Operating cash flow of 331 for nine months fiscal 2026 compares with 506 a year earlier. Receivable monetization programs sold 935 in the period and settled 935, leaving 65 outstanding, the same as at the start of the year, so the programs did not add net funding over nine months but remain a recurring working capital tool. Claims outside the debt figure include operating and finance leases, a 41 Kuwait court judgment under appeal that is not accrued, letters of credit and surety support, and a United Kingdom pension surplus rather than a deficit. The view is therefore moderate leverage, adequate liquidity, a near-term amortization step, an EBITDA definition that flatters the trend, and a covenant package that cannot be tested against defined terms.

Net debt = gross debt less cash of continuing operations (439, 312, 380, 500), giving 2,118, 2,258, 2,222 and 2,117, which equal the company's printed net debt at every date. Divided by TTM adjusted EBITDA (1,015, 987, 971, 968): gross 2.52, 2.60, 2.68, 2.70; net 2.09, 2.29, 2.29, 2.19. Inputs: debt tables for Jul 3 and Apr 3 are on [10-Q_2026-07-03_kbr-20260703.htm.jsonl, page:17] and [10-Q_2026-04-03_kbr-20260403.htm.jsonl, page:14]; cash for those dates on page:4 of each; net debt and TTM EBITDA at [EX-99.1_2026-07-30_q226kbr-exhibit991x07032026.htm.jsonl, page:2] for July 3, 2026 and at [EX-99.1_2026-05-05_q126kbr-exhibit991x04032026.htm.jsonl, page:1] and page:2 of the same release for April 3, 2026.
C2. Cash interest cover, fiscal 2025. Adjusted EBITDA 968 / cash paid for interest 141 = 6.87x. Interest expense of 158 gives 968 / 158 = 6.13x. Interim cash interest is Not supplied.

C3. Interest expense memo (not cash interest). TTM interest expense = fiscal 2025 (158) + current year to date less prior-year same period. Oct 2, 2026: 158 + 108 - 121 = 145; 1,015 / 145 = 7.00x. Jul 3, 2026: 158 + 72 - 82 = 148, where 72 is nine months (108) less Q3 (36) and 82 is nine months of 2025 (121) less Q3 of 2025 (39); 987 / 148 = 6.67x. Apr 3, 2026: 158 + 37 - 41 = 154 using the Q1 release interest expense of 37 and 41 on [EX-99.1_2026-05-05_q126kbr-exhibit991x04032026.htm.jsonl, page:12]; 971 / 154 = 6.31x.

C4. Definition sensitivity. Net debt 2,118 / (1,015 - 44 joint venture add-backs) = 2,118 / 971 = 2.18x, against 2.09x as printed. Letter of credit lines: bilateral 491 less 305 used = 186, and 607 + 186 = 793, which equals the 10-Q total remaining capacity of about 793 and confirms the 607 treatment. Inputs: [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:20] and the Q2, Q1 and annual equivalents at [10-Q_2026-07-03_kbr-20260703.htm.jsonl, page:20], [10-Q_2026-04-03_kbr-20260403.htm.jsonl, page:17] and [10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page:97].

The schedule is not updated for 2026 repayments: 301 on the revolver against 281 of borrowings, 29 on Term Loan A and 8 on Term Loan B.

C7. Derived fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 = fiscal 2025 less nine months of 2025: revenues 7,786 - 5,901 = 1,885; operating income 778 - 587 = 191; net income attributable to KBR 415 - 304 = 111; operating cash flow 557 - 506 = 51; adjusted EBITDA 968 - 730 = 238. C9. Segment arithmetic for scale (not a pro forma). Nine months fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA: MTS 441, Sustainable Technology Solutions 407, Corporate (71), consolidated 777. ### Business and transaction view

KBR, INC. is a listed company with no named sponsor and no parent: the context leaves those fields blank, the cover shows 126,108,987 shares outstanding at October 21, 2026, and the beneficial ownership table is incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not in the pack, so holder concentration and control rights are not supplied. The business has two core segments. Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) serves defense, intelligence, space and civil government customers, mainly in the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia, largely on cost-reimbursable terms; U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue and U.K. government customers 9%. Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) licenses proprietary process technology and provides engineering and advisory services to energy and chemicals customers, with a large equity-method joint venture component. The operating model is capital light, project and program based, and dependent on backlog conversion, working capital and joint venture distributions; backlog was 17,718 at October 2, 2026, plus 5,404 of award options, of which 38% is expected to be executed within one year, and nearly all contracts allow termination for convenience.

The transaction that dominates the credit view is the Planned Spin-Off of MTS into a separate listed company, to be named Trinzic, Inc., first announced in September 2025 and now targeted for January 4, 2027, the first business day of fiscal 2027, after the evidence cutoff. Completion is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing, and regulatory approvals. The mechanism that matters to creditors is that MTS is the larger segment by revenue, adjusted EBITDA and backlog, so after separation the remaining KBR group is the STS business plus corporate costs, while management says it will use cash distributed by MTS from its own financing to reduce KBR's debt. The size of that distribution, which debt stays with which company, whether the Senior Credit Facility and the Senior Notes remain with KBR, and the covenant and guarantor perimeter after separation are not supplied. The July 29, 2026 Amendment No. 14 to the credit agreement permits the internal reorganization; its text is not supplied. Behaviour to date is that of a company preparing a separation while keeping its dividend, cutting buybacks, and making small acquisitions and minority investments, with no documented priming, non-pro-rata exchange or distribution to insiders. The creditor view is therefore: a business with diversified government and commercial exposure, moderate leverage and large pending structural change, where the post-spin perimeter, debt allocation and covenant package, not the pre-spin credit statistics, will decide the credit quality, and where those facts are not yet in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The one transaction in the pack is the Planned Spin-Off of the Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business into Trinzic, Inc., announced in September 2025 and targeted for January 4, 2027, after the evidence cutoff. It is a spin-off to shareholders, not a sale, merger or sponsor transaction, so there is no purchase price, sponsor equity or acquisition financing. It is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or private letter ruling, effectiveness of the Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, satisfactory completion of financing and regulatory approvals. For creditors, the mechanism is that MTS makes a cash distribution to KBR from its own financing before completion, which management intends to use to reduce KBR's debt; the amount, the debt that stays with each company and the treatment of guarantors, liens and covenants are not supplied. Spin-off costs and other charges were 24 in the third quarter and 70 over nine months fiscal 2026. No new notes, term loan or other debt issue by KBR, INC. appears in the periods covered: the financing events are revolver borrowings of 281 and repayments of 301, scheduled repayments of 29 on Term Loan A and 8 on Term Loan B, and Amendment No. 14 to the Credit Agreement dated July 29, 2026, which permits internal reorganization transactions for the spin-off and makes other modifications that are not described. Management states that the spin-off is tax-free in intent, and that KBR and Trinzic expect to launch as independent companies in January, which is Management Language. Liquidity effects, debt maturities and covenant levels are in the financial base module. The earlier timing statement of the second half of fiscal 2026 was superseded by the January 4, 2027 target from the first quarter of fiscal 2026 onward, and is logged as a conflict below. Trinzic's own financing terms are Not supplied.

## Calculations
No financial figure is recomputed here; leverage, liquidity and maturity belong to the financial base module. Only shares of printed figures are computed, in US$ millions.

C1. Segment shares, nine months fiscal 2026 (inputs from [10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page:11] and [EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page:3]). MTS revenue 3,870 / consolidated revenue 5,935 = 65.2%. MTS adjusted EBITDA 441 / 777 = 56.8%; STS adjusted EBITDA 407 / 777 = 52.4%; Corporate (71) / 777 = -9.1%, sum 100.1% from rounding. C2. Equity earnings share. Equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates 167 / operating income 538 = 31.0% for nine months fiscal 2026; STS 130 of the 167 = 77.8%.

C3. Contract type shares, fiscal 2025 (page:140 of the annual report). Cost-reimbursable 3,305 / 7,786 = 42.4%; time-and-materials 2,311 / 7,786 = 29.7%; fixed price 2,170 / 7,786 = 27.9%. ### Credit view

KBR, INC. is a moderately levered, well-funded defense and sustainable-technology services group whose credit is sound on today's numbers but is about to be reset by the planned spin-off of its larger segment. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,046 million, net leverage of 2.1x on management's measure and a backlog of USD 17,718 million. The weakest point is that adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026, current maturities rose to USD 554 million, and no post-spin debt, covenant or guarantor terms are disclosed. The outcome turns on how much debt the Mission Technology Solutions cash distribution retires, how the August 2027 term loan is refinanced, and whether the remaining sustainable technology group can carry the capital structure it inherits.
### Credit assessment and thesis

Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium, held below High because the covenant, indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, the post-spin capital structure is Not supplied, and the business context was ready only with limitations. Basis: financial base leverage, liquidity, maturity and definition rows; business context transaction, customer concentration, backlog and governance rows.

Thesis: KBR, INC. can service and refinance its present debt from liquidity and recurring government and technology programs, but its credit quality will be decided by the debt, covenants and earnings base it carries after the Mission Technology Solutions spin-off, which the evidence does not yet show.
### Key findings

1. The spin-off, not the pre-spin ratios, drives the credit view (Documentary Fact for the facts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). The planned separation of Mission Technology Solutions into Trinzic, Inc. is targeted for January 4, 2027, after the cutoff, and is conditional on Board approval, tax treatment, a Form 10 filed on September 30, 2026, financing and regulatory approvals [business context, transaction register]. That segment carried USD 3,870 million of USD 5,935 million nine-month revenue and USD 441 million of USD 777 million nine-month adjusted EBITDA [business context, calculations], so what remains is the sustainable technology segment plus corporate costs, with USD 336 million of nine-month adjusted EBITDA on the same definition. Management intends to use cash distributed by the departing segment to reduce KBR's debt, but the amount, the allocation of existing debt, and the fate of guarantors and covenants are Not supplied [business context, gaps]. Credit implication: pre-spin leverage cannot be carried forward, and no post-spin leverage claim is made here.

2. Reported leverage is moderate but flattered by a definition change (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Net debt of USD 2,118 million over trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,015 million is 2.1x, against 2.2x at January 2, 2026, and gross leverage is 2.52x [financial base, leverage chart]. Since the first quarter of fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA adds back joint venture items of USD 44 million over nine months without recasting history; without them net leverage is 2.18x, almost level with 2.19x at the end of fiscal 2025, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization it is 2.37x [financial base, definition review]. Credit implication: most of the apparent improvement is definitional, so covenant judgments should use the lower-quality measures as well.

3. A refinancing and amortization step falls inside twelve months (Documentary Fact). Current maturities of long-term debt are USD 554 million at October 2, 2026 against USD 49 million at January 2, 2026, because Term Loan A-2 matures in August 2027; the USD 250 million Senior Notes mature in September 2028, and the revolver and Term Loan A-1 and A-3 in February 2029 [financial base, debt schedule]. Liquidity is USD 1,046 million, made of cash of USD 439 million and USD 607 million undrawn on the revolver after letters of credit, against the USD 625 million revolver capacity stated in the release [financial base, liquidity chart]. Credit implication: the tranche can be repaid from liquidity or refinanced, but its timing coincides with the separation, when lender consent, ratings and covenant terms are being reset (Amendment No. 14 already permitted the reorganization).

4. Covenant headroom cannot be tested (Insufficient Information). The filings describe a maximum consolidated net leverage ratio of 4.00x and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 3.00x, with compliance stated at every reported date, but the credit agreement, Amendment No. 14 and the indenture are Not supplied and the covenant ratios are not printed [financial base, covenants]. On the company basis the indicative figures are 2.09x net leverage and 7.00x adjusted EBITDA to interest expense. Credit implication: the cushion looks wide on any measure computed here, but it is indicative only, because defined terms and joint venture add-back treatment are unknown (see Calculations).

5. Cash conversion depends on working capital, joint venture distributions and receivable sales (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 331 million against USD 506 million a year earlier, a simple free cash flow build is USD 295 million, equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates was USD 167 million of operating income of USD 538 million (31.0%) against cash distributions of earnings of USD 145 million, and USD 935 million of receivables were sold and settled in the period, leaving USD 65 million outstanding, unchanged from the start of the year [financial base, claims outside debt; business context, calculations]. Cash interest paid is available for fiscal 2025 only, where adjusted EBITDA covered it 6.87x. Credit implication: debt service capacity is adequate on the evidence but rests on cash that KBR does not fully control, and the interim cash cover is Not supplied.

6. Customer concentration and budget timing shape revenue visibility (Documentary Fact). U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue and the U.K. government 9%; backlog was USD 17,718 million, 38% executable within one year, USD 9.0 billion of the departing segment's backlog is funded, nearly all contracts can be terminated for convenience, and a continuing resolution funds the U.S. government only to December 11, 2026 [business context, operating model]. Credit implication: revenue is visible but not contractual, and the concentration moves with the segment that is leaving, so the remaining group's profile is more commercial and more tied to energy and chemicals project cycles, which the evidence describes only in part.

7. Behaviour to date is not creditor-adverse on documented actions (Analyst Interpretation). Buybacks fell to USD 29 million over nine months from USD 304 million, the dividend was kept at USD 63 million, acquisitions were small in fiscal 2025, and no priming, uptier or leakage is documented; USD 177 million of minority and joint venture investments were made in nine months (USD 115 million in one joint venture, USD 49 million in securities and USD 13 million in other investments) [business context, governance]. Credit implication: discretionary cash returns are a lever management has used to conserve cash, but legal capacity under the credit agreement is untested and a post-spin capital allocation policy is Not supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity is a clear strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,046 million of cash and undrawn revolver, against a first scheduled tranche of USD 554 million and no maturity of the Senior Notes until September 2028 [financial base]. Leverage is moderate on every measure computed, from 2.1x as printed to 2.37x unadjusted, well below the described 4.00x covenant ceiling (Analyst Interpretation, indicative only). Revenue visibility from a backlog of USD 17,718 million, with USD 9.0 billion of the Mission Technology Solutions backlog funded and USD 5,404 million of award options (Documentary Fact) [business context]. Diversified end markets and geography beyond the U.S. government, with commercial and infrastructure clients and international government clients contributing USD 2,454 million and USD 905 million in fiscal 2025 (Documentary Fact). Cash returns are discretionary and have been reduced, with USD 402 million of repurchase authorization remaining, which gives management a lever in a stress (Analyst Interpretation). The management description of a low capital intensity model with favorable operating cash flows is Management Language and is not adopted; the financial base shows nine-month capital expenditure of USD 36 million against operating cash flow of USD 331 million, which is consistent with it.

Weaknesses. The post-spin capital structure is Not supplied (Insufficient Information): the debt allocation, the Senior Notes guarantor perimeter and covenants after separation determine the credit, and missing evidence is not treated as adverse. Adjusted EBITDA changed definition in 2026 and mixes two bases in its trailing figure (Documentary Fact). Near-term amortization and the August 2027 tranche arrive during the separation (Documentary Fact). Earnings include a large share of equity-method income (USD 167 million of USD 538 million of operating income) whose cash arrives only as distributions (Analyst Interpretation). Revenue is concentrated in one sovereign customer in the segment that leaves, and fiscal budgets run on continuing resolutions (Documentary Fact). Nine-month operating cash flow declined by USD 175 million to USD 331 million (Documentary Fact, from USD 506 million). Contingent items outside the debt figure include an unaccrued USD 41 million Kuwait court judgment under appeal and letters of credit of USD 18 million on the revolver and USD 305 million on bilateral lines (Documentary Fact). Interim cash interest is Not supplied and covenant definitions are Not supplied (Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Post-spin debt, covenant and guarantor perimeter undisclosed | The departing segment is the larger earnings contributor; where existing debt, the Senior Notes guarantees and the covenant package sit decides leverage and structural position after January 4, 2027 | Pre-spin credit metrics may not describe the surviving credit; a distribution smaller than expected would leave leverage higher on a smaller EBITDA base | Critical |

| Refinancing of Term Loan A-2 and current maturities of USD 554 million | The tranche matures in August 2027 inside twelve months, alongside the separation and covenant resets | Liquidity of USD 1,046 million covers it, but lender and rating conditions at separation could raise the cost or condition of refinancing | Material |

| Adjusted EBITDA quality and definition | Joint venture add-backs of USD 44 million, spin-off and restructuring add-backs of USD 72 million and equity earnings inflate the denominator of reported leverage | Reported 2.1x understates unadjusted leverage of 2.37x; covenant EBITDA may differ | Material |
| Covenant opacity | Defined terms, amendment effects and add-back treatment are not supplied | Headroom cannot be verified; a sharp earnings drop could breach unseen tests | Material |

| Government concentration and budget timing | 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue from the U.S. government, funding on a continuing resolution to December 11, 2026, contracts terminable for convenience | Award and cash conversion delays could depress cash flow before and after separation | Material |

| Cash conversion and off-balance items | Receivable sales of USD 935 million in nine months, joint venture distributions, letters of credit, a USD 41 million unaccrued judgment | Cash flow depends on programs and counterparties outside the debt figure | Material |

| Interest rate exposure after swap expiry | Variable debt of USD 748 million after swaps; swaps of USD 400 million and USD 350 million run to January 2027 | Higher base rates raise interest cost; USD 6 million for a 50 basis point rise on current exposure | Minor |
## Calculations
All amounts are USD millions. Inputs are taken from the financial base and business context handoffs and are not re-read from sources; results are indicative arithmetic, not forecasts.

C1. Lower-quality leverage measures (inputs from the financial base). Net debt 2,118 / trailing adjusted EBITDA 1,015 = 2.09x as printed; 2,118 / (1,015 - 44) = 2,118 / 971 = 2.18x; 2,118 / 895 = 2.37x on trailing operating income plus depreciation and amortization of 895.

C2. EBITDA cushion to the described covenant levels (company basis, indicative). Net leverage ceiling 4.00x: EBITDA could fall to 2,118 / 4.00 = 529.5, a decline of 1,015 - 529.5 = 485.5, or 47.8%. Interest coverage floor 3.00x on the memo interest expense of 145: required EBITDA 3.00 x 145 = 435, a decline of 580, or 57.1%. Defined terms are not supplied, so these are not covenant headroom.
C3. Liquidity against the nearest maturity. Liquidity 439 + 607 = 1,046; current maturities 554; 1,046 / 554 = 1.89x.

C4. Scale of the perimeter change (illustrative, not a forecast or pro forma). Nine-month adjusted EBITDA excluding the departing segment: 407 - 71 = 336, or 336 / 777 = 43.2% of the consolidated figure. Applying that share to trailing net debt gives 2,118 x 336 / 777 = 916, so holding net leverage at 2.09x would require net debt to fall by about 2,118 - 916 = 1,202. The share is from nine-month figures and net debt is at a point in time; corporate cost allocation after separation, stranded costs, the debt the new company assumes and the size of the cash distribution are Not supplied.
C5. Sensitivity of leverage to debt repayment. Each 100 of net debt repaid reduces net leverage by 100 / 1,015 = 0.10x on the printed basis.

C6. Cash flow and investment sums. Nine-month operating cash flow 506 - 331 = 175 lower. Minority and joint venture investments 115 + 49 + 13 = 177. Letters of credit outside the debt figure: 18 on the revolver and 305 on bilateral lines.

| G2 | Credit agreement, Amendment No. 14 and the Senior Notes indenture are Not supplied; covenant ratios are not printed | Covenant headroom and legal capacity for distributions cannot be tested | Key findings 4 and 7 | High | Add the executed documents and compliance certificates |

| G3 | Adjusted EBITDA definition changed in 2026 and was not recast; fiscal 2025 reconciliation is not in the pack | Trailing leverage mixes two bases | Key finding 2 | High | Obtain the fiscal 2025 reconciliation; show both bases |

| G4 | Interim 2026 cash interest and cash taxes are Not supplied | Cash interest cover is available for fiscal 2025 only | Key finding 5 | Medium | Use fiscal 2025 cover and the labelled interest expense memo |

| G5 | Ownership percentages and control rights are Not supplied (proxy statement not in the pack) | Control and alignment cannot be assessed | Key finding 7 | Medium | Add the proxy statement; no percentage is inferred |
| G6 | No ratings or agency commentary in the sources or context | Ratings events at separation cannot be considered | Credit view | Medium | Not supplied; do not infer |

| G7 | Context period labels q2-2027 and fy-2026 match no source; the latest quarter is the third quarter of fiscal 2026 | Period labelling | All findings | Medium | Confirm the intended periods with the requester |

| G8 | Readiness handoff recorded no stand-alone fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 source and a revolver capacity basis difference between the release (USD 625 million) and the 10-Q (USD 607 million after letters of credit) | Minor comparability effects | Liquidity | Low | Use the 10-Q basis and state it |
## Next module

Proceed with evidence-trace validation (CP-5). Pass forward: the credit view is moderate leverage and strong liquidity today, with the post-spin perimeter, debt allocation, covenants and guarantors Not supplied; use the financial base figures by label (net leverage 2.09x printed, 2.18x without joint venture add-backs, 2.37x unadjusted proxy; liquidity USD 1,046 million using the 10-Q basis of USD 607 million undrawn; current maturities USD 554 million); trace each key finding to its financial base or business context row, including the indicative covenant cushion in the calculations, which depends on undefined terms; treat the January 4, 2027 spin-off date, the investor days and the distribution intent as targets or Management Language after the cutoff; and keep the Critical gap on the post-spin capital structure visible in every conclusion.

## Calculations

Leverage inputs were recomputed from lines extracted separately from the filing pages, not from the figures typed in the modules; liquidity, bridge and schedule figures were recomputed from inputs checked against the pages. All reproduced. Amounts are USD millions.

- Gross debt (Term Loan A + Term Loan B + Senior Notes + Revolver): 957 + 975 + 250 + 375 = 2,557 (Oct 2, 2026); 967 + 978 + 250 + 375 = 2,570 (Jul 3, 2026); 977 + 980 + 250 + 395 = 2,602 (Apr 3, 2026); 989 + 983 + 250 + 395 = 2,617 (Jan 2, 2026). Less cash 439, 312, 380 and 500: net debt 2,118, 2,258, 2,222 and 2,117, equal to the printed net debt at every date.
- Leverage: gross 2.52, 2.60, 2.68, 2.70 and net 2.09, 2.29, 2.29, 2.19, in line with the printed 2.1x, 2.3x, 2.3x and 2.2x.
- Carrying-value basis (difference of 16 of issuance costs at Oct 2, 2026): 2,541 / 1,015 = 2.50x gross; 2,541 - 439 = 2,102 and 2,102 / 1,015 = 2.07x net.

- Liquidity: 1,000 - 375 - 18 = 607; 439 + 607 = 1,046; 305 on bilateral lines of 491 leaves 186, and 607 + 186 = 793, equal to the printed total remaining capacity. The same check ties at the other three dates: 588 + 200 = 788; 607 + 201 = 808; 591 + 192 = 783.

- Working capital check, nine months fiscal 2026 against nine months fiscal 2025: receivables (218) against (40), contract assets (38) against 29, accounts payable 134 against (52), contract liabilities 99 against (1), accrued salaries 19 against 41; the five lines sum to (4) against (23). Operating cash flow fell by 506 - 331 = 175, while other assets and liabilities moved from 59 to (107), a swing of 166, and distributions of earnings from 163 to 145, a fall of 18. The working capital lines did not drive the decline.

- Non-debt funding float: contract liabilities 429 against 331 at Jan 2, 2026 and accounts payable 847 against 712, so customer advances and payables funded part of the working capital; sold receivables outstanding were 65 at both dates.
- Add-back check: 538 - 4 + 126 + 72 + 44 + 1 = 777 for nine months fiscal 2026.
- Without JV add-backs: 2,118 / 971 = 2.18x.
- Limitation: recomputation uses the same company definitions as the modules, so it tests arithmetic and sourcing, not the definitions or the covenant terms.
